neighbours.label: 'a high'/'a higher' before a rate or risk noun (a high risk of bleeding, a higher return rate)
fire: Smokers face a high risk of developing lung disease later in life.
The new treatment showed a higher survival rate than the older drug.
Older cars carry a higher chance of breaking down in winter.
Teenage drivers have a high rate of accidents at night.
Premature babies show a higher incidence of breathing problems.
This region has a high likelihood of flooding every autumn.
Patients on the drug had a higher rate of liver damage.
Startups face a high probability of failure in their first year.
quiet: Smokers often develop lung disease later in life, doctors say.
The new treatment helped more patients survive than the older drug.
Older cars often break down in winter when the roads are icy.
Teenage drivers cause many accidents at night on rural roads.
Premature babies often have breathing problems in their first weeks.
This region often floods in autumn after heavy rain.
Some patients on the drug developed liver damage after a year.
Many startups fail in their first year for lack of money.

predictions: Fires on 'high'/'higher' (or the article before it) when it sets up a rate, risk or propensity noun, in medical and non-medical text alike; plain clinical description without that phrasing stays lower.
notes: Probe: 'presents with a high risk of bleeding' 0.640; 'a higher return rate' (finance) 0.333; 'a higher death rate' 0.270; clinical description without that phrasing 0.088-0.112; non-medical control 0.033. The card's medical framing looks secondary. Low confidence.
